stemBlocks.value: Make n the subject of the formula m = n − 4.
Think first: The 4 is being subtracted from n, so add it back to both sides.

stemBlocks.altText: Source visual for edmar-csec-p095-q02 from workbook page 95.

solutionSteps.instruction: Write the new subject on the left.

strategyBlocks.value: Add 4 to both sides to isolate n, then write the formula with n as the subject.

whyThisWorks.value: Addition and subtraction undo each other. Adding 4 to both sides removes the −4 attached to n while keeping the two sides equal, so the rearranged formula describes exactly the same relationship as the original.

commonErrors.misconception: Writing n = m − 4, copying the original sign.
commonErrors.correctiveNote: Avoid this: Writing n = m − 4, copying the original sign.

commonErrors.misconception: Adding 4 to the n side only.
commonErrors.correctiveNote: Avoid this: Adding 4 to the n side only.

commonErrors.misconception: Changing the letters round as well as the sign, giving m = n + 4.
commonErrors.correctiveNote: Avoid this: Changing the letters round as well as the sign, giving m = n + 4.

examTip.value: Say the operation out loud as you undo it — 'n has 4 taken off, so I add 4' — which stops sign slips before they happen.
